dedupe_keys.name: jammertest annual open gnss jamming spoofing and meaconing test at andøya with test catalogues and participant datasets

description: Jammertest is an annual event at Andøya in northern Norway, run with the Norwegian Public Roads Administration, the Norwegian Communications Authority, the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment, the Norwegian Metrology Service, the Norwegian Space Agency and Testnor, and described as the largest open PNT and GNSS resilience test in the world. Participants bring receivers, vehicles, drones and aircraft to four test areas, including an airport, where organisers transmit scheduled jamming, spoofing and meaconing at set powers and bands. The organisers publish the test plan and catalogue, with times, locations and signal settings of every test, on GitHub (NPRA/jammertest-plan), and participants deposit recordings made during the tests; one example is Université Gustave Eiffel's Jammertest 2024 dataset of raw UBX, RINEX, RF monitoring and navigation solutions from static and moving receivers (Zenodo, 0.38 GB, GPL-3.0). Coverage: Andøya, Norway, yearly since the early 2020s, most recently September 2026. Format and access: test catalogue files on GitHub and participant datasets on Zenodo and elsewhere, free of charge under each depositor's licence. Caveats: controlled attacks, not incidents; participant datasets differ in receivers and formats; the catalogue is needed to label them. Simulation uses: ground truth for testing interference detection, receiver resilience and the effect of GNSS loss on transport and timing systems. Related records: OAKBAT and the Fraunhofer highway interference data are other labelled sets; GPSJam maps real-world interference.
